# Transferring a solver correction space {#sec-solver-spaces}

**A frozen correction space fitted on source geometries transfers worse than
a free geometric coarse grid on every held-out discrete elliptic system
tested, so the direction stops for that class.** The audit's fourth
direction proposed learning a coarse correction space or preconditioner on
source problems and letting the correct target operator finish the solve,
the reasoning being that slow error modes might transfer more reliably than
whole fields. The nonlearned probe asked whether *any* frozen source-derived
space beats an equally cheap classical one; if not, a network trained to
produce such a space would start behind a construction that costs nothing to
learn. It does not.

## The probe {#sec-solver-probe}

Linear finite elements on the unit square with circular Neumann holes and a
piecewise-constant coefficient inclusion; Dirichlet data lifted and
eliminated so the diffusion operator is symmetric positive definite (about
2,000–2,200 unknowns). Twenty source geometries; three held-out sets of eight
each: new hole positions within the family, a topology shift (two holes, or a
hole two to three cells from the wall), and a tenfold larger coefficient
contrast. Correction spaces of dimension 16 and 32: a frozen proper
orthogonal decomposition of source errors that survive three damped-Jacobi
sweeps (ten smooth right-hand sides per source geometry, registered to a
shared background grid), a per-target oracle decomposition of the same kind
(an upper bound, not deployable), and three classical spaces of the same
dimension (piecewise-constant aggregation, smoothed aggregation, a bilinear
geometric coarse grid). Readouts: the energy-norm error left after one
Galerkin coarse correction on random, slow (generalized eigenvectors 4–20)
and near-null (eigenvectors 1–3) error directions; and complete two-level
conjugate-gradient solves to a relative residual of 10⁻⁸ with setup
amortized over ten right-hand sides. Bars, written before the run: advance
only if the frozen source space halves the slow-mode error left by the best
classical space within family and improves it by 1.5x under the topology
shift, and saves at least 20% of total work; stop if a classical space
matches or beats it on either held-out set
(`studies/solver_spaces/PREREG.md`).

## What the probe found {#sec-solver-result}

``` {.python .cell-code}
import json
from pathlib import Path
s = json.loads(Path("studies/solver_spaces/solver_spaces_summary.json").read_text())
```


| rank | held-out set | frozen source space | best classical space | classical ÷ source (bar ≥ 2.0 / ≥ 1.5) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | within family | 0.963 | 0.701 (geometric) | 0.73 |
| 16 | topology shift | 0.964 | 0.706 (geometric) | 0.73 |
| 16 | coefficient shift | 0.961 | 0.732 (geometric) | 0.76 |
| 32 | within family | 0.748 | 0.465 (geometric) | 0.62 |
| 32 | topology shift | 0.754 | 0.470 (geometric) | 0.62 |
| 32 | coefficient shift | 0.801 | 0.527 (geometric) | 0.66 |

: Energy-norm error left on slow-mode probes after one coarse correction,
mean over eight held-out geometries (lower is better). The rank-16
comparison is dimension-exact; at rank 32 the geometric grid has 36
columns. Diffusion operator. Data: `studies/solver_spaces/solver_spaces_summary.json`. {#tbl-solver-contraction}

On near-null probes at rank 32 the frozen space leaves 0.53 of the error,
the oracle 0.42, the geometric grid 0.37. In complete solves the frozen
space needs 141–162 iterations at rank 16 against 82–99 for the best
classical space and 84–104 against 61–72 at rank 32; counting setup, it
saves between −19% and −72% of the work, so no break-even number of
right-hand sides exists. Every solve converged; on the symmetric problem
residual and energy-norm error contract together, so the residual-not-error
failure the audit warned of does not arise here.

The mechanism is visible in the source spectrum. The smoother-resistant
source errors are low-dimensional (normalized singular values 0.10, 0.06,
0.04, 0.02 at modes 2, 5, 9, 17), but their span is that of the smooth
right-hand sides used to generate them around twenty particular hole
positions, not the target operator's slow subspace. The geometric grid
spans generic smooth functions, which is the slow space of a discrete
elliptic operator under a point smoother, for any geometry, without seeing
a source problem. Even the oracle decomposition fitted on the target's own
smoothed errors leaves 0.78 of the slow-mode error against the grid's 0.47.
Solution snapshots are the wrong object to fit a correction space from, and
a learner trained on them inherits the mismatch.

The convection–diffusion variant was run and is reported as not measured:
at mesh Péclet 0.5 the preconditioned GMRES converges in two to three
iterations with any space, and the one-step Galerkin correction is not a
projection for a nonsymmetric operator (it increases the slow-mode error
for the fitted spaces). A Petrov–Galerkin correction and a higher Péclet
number would be needed for that case to discriminate.

## What this changes {#sec-solver-consequence}

The direction stops for discrete elliptic problems on a fixed
discretization: a learned correction space must beat the geometric coarse
grid, not the absence of one, and the object to learn would have to be
operator-aware (near-null vectors of the *target* operator, which adaptive
algebraic multigrid already computes without learning) rather than fitted
to source solutions. Two homes remain for a learned solver component, and
each needs a prerequisite gate before any training: operators whose
classical coarse spaces demonstrably fail (strong anisotropy, indefinite or
high-Péclet operators, state-dependent nonlinear Jacobians, where the
audit's nonlinear extension lives), and learned smoothers or prolongation
weights on a classical hierarchy, which are a different object from a
frozen space. Chapter @sec-classical-solvers takes up the second as part of
the question of what classical solvers do that surrogates do not.
